bib.title: Learning without training: The implicit dynamics of in-context learning

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Learning without training: The implicit dynamics of in-context learning", Benoit Dherin*, Michael Munn*, Hanna Mazzawi*, Michael Wunder, Javier Gonzalvo (Google Research). arXiv:2507.16003v4 [cs.CL], 2 Jun 2026 (the printed date). Preprint, filed as 2025.

COVERAGE: 24 of 24 pages read, 70443 of 70443 chars (body, references, appendices A-D). The text extracted cleanly. I did not run the figures script. The figure captions below come from the extracted text. Equations are partly garbled but readable.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: A forward pass with context equals a forward pass without context, with the first MLP weight matrix patched by a rank-1 update. The paper calls this the minimal token-patch.
  number: rank 1; the update is the unique Frobenius-norm minimiser
  setup: Theorem 2.3 (exact algebra, not an empirical result). It covers a contextual layer (self-attention is the example) followed by an MLP. It matches pre-activations of the first dense layer. It requires A(C\Y,x) != 0. Appendix C.2 extends it to skip connections, LayerNorm and stacked blocks.
  quote: "a forward pass with context isfunctionally equivalent—identical in output—to adifferent computationthat is never performed on the hardware: one in which a weight update replaces the prompt context."
  where: p.2 (intro)
- claim: The update formula is delta·vᵀ/||v||², where v = A(C\Y,x) and delta = W times the context vector. The update is "conservative": W is unchanged in every direction orthogonal to A(C\Y,x).
  number: Eq. 3
  setup: Single block without skip connection. The update depends on the query token x.
  quote: "Δ𝑥𝑊(𝑌)= (𝑊𝛿𝐴𝑥(𝑌))𝐴(𝐶\𝑌,𝑥) 𝑇 ∥𝐴(𝐶\𝑌,𝑥)∥ 2" and "it preserves the original weights𝑊 in all directions orthogonal to𝐴(𝐶\𝑌,𝑥)"
  where: p.4, Theorem 2.3
- claim: With skip connections, the context also gives an exact bias patch, equal to the context vector. This is functionally an activation steering vector. The weight part resembles ROME/MEND factual edits, and the bias part resembles steering/task vectors.
  number: none
  setup: Theorem C.2, stacks of L pre-LN blocks.
  quote: "For each layer𝑙=1,...,𝐿, the exact bias-patch is given by the layer's context vector" and "our work connects steering vectors and low-rank matrix edits to the implicit mechanisms of the transformer architecture."
  where: p.2 and p.20-21
- claim: Consuming prompt tokens one at a time is equivalent to an online gradient-descent-like sequence of weight updates. Each token acts like a data point. The learning rate is 1/||A(x)||², and the update vanishes when a token has no marginal effect on the output.
  number: h = 1/||A(x)||²
  setup: Proposition 2.6. The authors concede this is "an algebraic consequence of the additive structure": any additive update can be written as a gradient step on a linear loss (Remark 2.7).
  quote: "learning rate given byℎ= 1/∥𝐴(𝑥)∥ 2 and loss at step𝑖given by 𝐿 𝑖(𝑊)=trace(Δ 𝑇𝑖𝑊)" and "any sequence𝑊𝑖+1 =𝑊 𝑖+𝐺 𝑖 can be written as𝑊𝑖+1 =𝑊 𝑖−ℎ∇ 𝑊𝐿𝑖(𝑊𝑖)"
  where: p.5
- claim: In a linear-attention toy setup with hand-chosen weights, the implicit dynamics equals exactly one step of full-batch gradient descent on a least-squares loss. This is an existence proof only.
  number: one GD step
  setup: Single linear MLP layer, linear attention, W=[w0,-1], in-context linear regression, following von Oswald et al. 2023.
  quote: "the implicit learning dynamics is exactly equivalent to one step of full-batch Gradient Descent with learning rate𝜂 on the weights𝜔0."
  where: p.6
- claim: The equivalence holds numerically in a deep network, with block outputs agreeing to about 1e-6.
  number: 1e-6; 10 layers; 100 test tasks
  setup: 10-layer pre-LN transformer with LayerNorm and residuals, trained on in-context linear regression. d_model=32, d_mlp=128, 8 heads, Adam lr 0.001, d=2, context length 100, batch 32.
  quote: "The intermediate block outputs agree to a precision of10−6, confirming our theoretical framework perfectly captures the mechanics of the forward pass in deep networks."
  where: p.7 (3.1), App. D.1-D.2 p.24
- claim: The implicit weight update tracks explicit SGD finetuning of the MLP on the same examples. Test loss falls similarly, and the normalised Frobenius inner product stays between roughly 0.95 and 1.0 (read from the Fig. 2 axis).
  number: axis range 0.95-1.00 (read off the plot; the text gives no figure)
  setup: Single-layer transformer (L=1), linear regression, SGD with a tuned learning rate, one example per step, context length up to 100.
  quote: "both the implicit dynamics and explicit finetuning minimize the test loss in remarkably similar ways." and "the implicit weight updates and explicit SGD gradients remain highly aligned in weight space."
  where: p.7-8, App. D.3
- claim: As a diagnostic, attention-based contextual layers give implicit updates that decay and converge. RNN layers give unstable, non-converging updates. The authors offer this as an explanation for why RNNs do worse at ICL.
  number: none (qualitative; the RNN plot y-range is about 1.0-1.4)
  setup: Attention layer swapped for an RNN with d_model=64, d_mlp=128, lr 0.005, 10,000 steps. Context length 100-200. One run, linear regression.
  quote: "For Attention-based layers, the implicit gradient updates smoothly decay and converge to zero, indicating stable assimilation of the context. Conversely, the RNN's implicit updates fail to converge, exhibiting highly unstable dynamics."
  where: p.8
- claim: A single static "thought patch" can approximate the context for prompt compression. It is fitted by least squares over K calibration queries. It generalises to held-out queries as K grows. The authors say it could enable O(1) inference without a KV-cache; this is not demonstrated.
  number: K in {1,2,5,10,25,50,100}; 100 held-out test queries
  setup: Single-layer transformer block, in-context linear regression, one fixed context. Metrics are MSE and the mean difference between patched and full output. The exact error values appear only in Fig. 4, with no numbers in the text.
  quote: "𝐾∈{ 1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100}" and "transitions from an overfit solution for specific queries (at low𝐾) to a robust, query-agnostic approximation that generalizes to unseen tokens (for large values of𝐾)."
  where: p.9 (3.4.1) and Fig. 4 p.10
- claim: The result does not depend on softmax or single-head attention. Any layer that takes an input and an optional context qualifies. Earlier theory needed linear attention, a single head, or special prompt forms.
  number: none
  setup: Theory only. Experiments use attention and an RNN.
  quote: "our main Theorems (Thm. 2.3 and Thm. C.2) remain valid if the self-attention layer is switched by other forms of contextual layers, such an RNNs, state space models, or any layer that can take an input and optionally a context."
  where: p.9-10
- claim: Context can be compressed exactly into MLP weights but not exactly into attention weights, so the paper suggests the feedforward network is the "reservoir" for context adaptation. This contrasts with Chen et al. 2024, who prove exact ICL-to-weights conversion is impossible for linearized attention.
  number: none
  setup: Theoretical argument against Chen et al. (ICML 2024).
  quote: "the MLP layers do not. We show that the effect of the context can be mapped exactly to a low-rank update of the MLP weights in standard transformers, suggesting that the feedforward network acts as a natural reservoir for context-dependent weight adaptation."
  where: p.17 (App. A)
- claim: The authors propose a path to a formal theory of prompt engineering. Prompt segments map to linear operators, and concatenation maps to operator composition: W_n = W_0(I+h1A1)...(I+hnAn). They only suggest studying invertibility and commutativity; they do not test it.
  number: Eq. 33
  setup: Appendix C.2 / Corollary C.3 (the main text calls it Eq. 33), exact algebra.
  quote: "rigorously map prompt segments to linear operators and textual concatenation to operator composition." and "lays the groundwork for a formal theory of prompt engineering, moving beyond trial-and-error"
  where: p.10 and p.23
- claim: Related-work framing of ICL. It is either Bayesian conditioning / retrieval of pretrained skill (Xie 2022, Reynolds & McDonell 2021, Min 2022 with random labels), or genuine learning that depends on scale and data diversity (Wei 2024, Raventos 2023).
  number: none
  setup: Literature summary only; no new experiments.
  quote: "Min et al. (2022) shows that replacing example labels with random labels does not dramatically decrease ICL performance" and "Wei et al. (2024) show that these results may in fact vary depending on model size and that larger models do start to actually learn from switched labels within the prompt."
  where: p.16

LIMITS
- All experiments are toy: in-context linear regression, feature dimension d=2, small transformers (10 layers at most, d_model 32 or 64). There are no pretrained LLMs and no natural-language prompts. The abstract's "LLM" framing is not tested.
- The authors concede the work is "mainly theoretical". The equivalence is mathematical: "this weight update is never directly computed"; it is not what the hardware does.
- The context vector is counterfactual. It needs A(C) and A(C\Y), and is "not a quantity that the model computes in a single forward pass" (Remark 2.4).
- The equivalence only matches pre-activations of the first MLP layer. It is stated as an "intractable and ill-posed" alternative otherwise.
- The patch is token-dependent, so the context "cannot be exactly represented by a single, fixed weight update". The static thought patch is a least-squares approximation, tested only at small scale.
- The gradient-descent reading is an algebraic reformulation (Remark 2.7). The match to explicit least squares is shown only under linear attention with hand-picked weights. For general nonlinear architectures it is "analytically intractable (and beyond the scope of this paper)".
- The attention-versus-RNN diagnostic is one small setup. The paper reads no more than "superior convergence" into it.
- Dated: v4 is of 2 Jun 2026. It cites a follow-up, Goldwaser et al., "Equivalence of context and parameter updates in modern transformer blocks" (arXiv 2511.17864), which covers modern blocks. The statement that RNNs "struggle with ICL" is asserted, not cited.
- Hallucination and mode-collapse detection via monitoring meta-gradients is listed as future work only.

BUILDS ON (as printed)
- von Oswald et al., 2023 (Transformers learn in-context by gradient descent); Dai et al., 2023 (GPT as meta-optimizers); Akyürek et al., 2023; Garg et al., 2022; Zhang, Frei & Bartlett, 2024; Ahn et al., 2023; Huang et al., 2025.
- Task and steering vectors: Ilharco et al., 2022; Hendel et al., 2023; Todd et al., 2023/2024.
- Model editing: Meng et al., 2022 (ROME, rank-1); Mitchell et al., 2022 (MEND).
- Chen et al., 2024 (exact ICL-to-weights conversion in linearized attention).
- Bayesian / retrieval views: Xie et al., 2022; Reynolds & McDonell, 2021; Min et al., 2022; Wei et al., 2024; Raventos et al., 2023.
- Brown et al., 2020 (GPT-3, few-shot learning); Vaswani et al., 2017; He & Hofmann, 2024 (pre-LN block form); Conmy 2023, Elhage 2021 and Olah 2020 (circuits, as a contrast); Vig et al., 2020 (causal mediation).

CODE: none in the source. Key formula, for the note:
- Eq. 3: "Δ𝑥𝑊(𝑌)= (𝑊𝛿𝐴𝑥(𝑌))𝐴(𝐶\𝑌,𝑥) 𝑇 ∥𝐴(𝐶\𝑌,𝑥)∥ 2", with "𝛿𝐴𝑥(𝑌):=𝐴(𝐶,𝑥)−𝐴(𝐶\𝑌,𝑥)" (p.4)
- Eq. 33: "𝑊𝑛 =𝑊 0(𝐼+ℎ 1𝐴1)(𝐼+ℎ 2𝐴2)···(𝐼+ℎ 𝑛𝐴𝑛)." (p.23)

FIGURES (captions from the text; I did not run the figures script)
- Fig. 1 (p.7): "Numerical Verification in 10-layer Pre-LN Transformer ... Predictions agree to an order of10−6." Shows that the equivalence is exact and not an approximation.
- Fig. 2 (p.8): "Direct finetuning vs implicit weight update. Left: Both finetuning and implicit weight updates minimize the loss in similar ways. Right: ... highly aligned with respect to the normalized Frobenius inner product". Best candidate for the idea "the prompt acts like a fine-tune".
- Fig. 3 (p.8): "Architectural Diagnostics. Left: Attention-based contextual layers produce smooth, converging implicit weight updates. Right: RNN-based ... highly unstable, non-converging updates". Gives a quick visual contrast.
- Fig. 4 (p.10): "Generalization of the static 'Thought Patch' Δ(C) across calibration set sizes K". Left: patched output converges to the full pass as K grows. Right: MSE approaches the full-context model.
- Best for note 01: Fig. 2, plus a hand-drawn diagram of "context -> rank-1 patch of W" built from Eq. 3.

Math symbols in the extraction are garbled (subscripts and fractions run together), so quotes containing equations are hard to read, though they match the extraction verbatim. Figure data points cannot be read from the text; numeric values for Figs. 2-4 are not given. The 0.95-1.00 range is from axis labels only.
